headline: US stocks ended mixed as AI revenue concerns pressured chipmakers while oil gains on Middle East risks lifted energy and firm labor data kept yields elevated
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) fell 0.47% to 7,765.36, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) rose 0.10% to 51,231.64, and the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) dropped 1.25% to 27,193.34.
- Chip stocks declined after the Financial Times reported OpenAI’s annualized revenue was $20 billion below prior signals, with Nvidia (NVDA) down nearly 3%, Intel (INTC) off 5.3%, Micron Technology (MU) down over 4%, AMD (AMD) nearly 4% lower, and the broader chip sector off 3.4%.
- Oracle (ORCL) fell more than 5% as part of the broader technology selloff tied to AI revenue concerns.
- Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG) rose 6.2% to $32.68 after reports that Starbucks (SBUX) had explored acquiring the chain, while Starbucks (SBUX) declined 0.4%.
- Energy names outperformed as oil (@CL) prices climbed on a fresh tanker attack in the Middle East, U.S. output cuts, and Hurricane Isaias threatening about 500,000 barrels per day of refining capacity.
- U.S. initial jobless claims held near a 57-year low for a fourth straight week, underscoring continued labor-market strength.
- The 10-year Treasury yield rose intraday before closing near 5.23%, while a 30-year Treasury auction passed a key test of investor confidence.
- PepsiCo (PEP) beat estimates with Q3 EPS of $2.34 versus $2.30 expected as it faces pressure from shifting eating habits and weighs options including a potential split.
- Investors looked ahead to Delta Air Lines (DAL)’ earnings and the University of Michigan consumer sentiment data due Friday.
